explanation: Fires on the word right after a short preposition-like prefix when the two make a fixed unit. The strongest case is a bare noun or adverb completing an ' at'/' in'/' as' idiom with no determiner between: ' once' in 'at once' (~2.1-2.6, while 'once' alone or 'only once' is <0.5), ' times' in 'at times', ' first', ' night', ' school', ' random', ' sea', ' large', ' place'/' time'/' front'/' advance' after ' in', ' often' after ' as'. The other case is the second piece of a split word after a short space-prefixed prefix: ' in'+'sec'(urities), ' in'+'ve'(ce), ' under'+'ton'(es), ' step'+'son', ' As'+'im'(ov), ' at'+'an'(2), plus text-initial 'Per'(cy), 'At', 'In'. Predicted inactive: (a) ordinary everyday English sentences of whole common words with no such idiom or split word, e.g. 'My brother bought a new car last week.' (24 tested, all peaks <=0.45); (b) ' at'/' in' followed by a determiner or possessive ('at the station', 'in a drawer', 'in my bag'; 16 tested, all peaks <=0.54). Some ' at X' idioms stay weak: 'at least', 'at last', 'at home', 'at all', 'at noon', 'in fact', 'in particular', 'in trouble' (all <0.35).
